A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StruMamba3D and contain readable text, equations, figures, and tables. v1 ends with references; v3 retains the main paper and adds an appendix. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original classification, part-segmentation, few-shot classification, and ablation results for StruMamba3D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ScanNetV2 detection results, further ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in the appendix.

M1.justification: The spatial states, position-dependent state updates, lightweight convolutions, bidirectional processing, adaptive sampling interval, and consistency loss remain unchanged. Appendix Algorithm 1 expands implementation documentation of the existing block; the new detection experiment does not establish a revised core method.

E1.justification: Section 9.2 adds training and evaluation on ScanNetV2 for large-scale scene-level 3D object detection. This substantially extends the earlier object-level classification, few-shot classification, and part-segmentation coverage, which is retained.

E2.justification: New Table 9 adds 3DETR and 3DETR-m as detection comparators alongside Point-M2AE. Comparator membership in the original classification, segmentation, and few-shot tables remains unchanged, making this a focused extension of the baseline set.

E3.justification: The added detection evaluation introduces 2048 input tokens, 128 spatial states, 1080 pretraining epochs, batch size 16, and mAP25/mAP50 metrics. Figures 4–5 also introduce token-length sweeps for computational cost and inference speed. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish changes to their protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v3 adds serialization comparisons, spatial-state-count and convolution-neighborhood sensitivity studies, and training without pretraining. It also adds efficiency scaling analyses and visual studies of state correlations, reconstruction, and segmentation, substantially broadening validation.

E5.justification: Both versions report few-shot means and standard deviations over 10 independent experiments. The appendix repeats that practice; it introduces no additional seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results. New results include 67.8 mAP25 and 50.6 mAP50 on ScanNetV2, per-category segmentation scores, sensitivity results, training-from-scratch scores, and efficiency curves. Table 8 separately reports official-code reproductions of PointGPT-S and PointMamba; their original Table 2 scores remain, so these are additional results rather than established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 and the SSM reasoning remain unchanged. Appendix Equations 14–15 explicitly state standard classification and segmentation cross-entropy losses; no substantive new mathematical definitions, derivations, assumptions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same structural-modeling and sequence-length-adaptation contributions, novelty claim, and headline accuracies. The appendix adds supporting evidence without redefining the main claims.

C2.justification: v1 already discusses potential benefits of multi-scale designs. Section 11 adds a specific failure condition—unclear segmentation boundaries—attributes it to single-scale features, and proposes hierarchical Mamba as future work. The appendix also adds interpretations of state specialization and hyperparameter sensitivity.

D1.justification: v1 provides basic architectural and sampling settings but defers further details. Section 8 and Algorithm 1 add tensor dimensions, block operations, downstream heads, optimizer and scheduler settings, training budgets, warm-up, voting details, and pretraining hardware and runtime: one RTX A6000 and approximately 18 hours. These substantially improve documentation of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Adam, SGDR, and additional 3D detection and representation-learning works. The related-work discussion and positioning against point-based, Transformer-based, and Mamba-based approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The original narrative and section order are largely unchanged. v3 updates author/contact information, adds an acknowledgment and an organized appendix, and makes small caption and cross-reference edits. Implementation explanations expand, but the main paper is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8–12, an unnumbered pretraining comparison table, Algorithm 1, and Figures 4–8. These include efficiency plots and extensive qualitative displays. The original figures and tables largely retain their presentation, but the added displays substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited implementation documentation and lack of large-scene evaluation and quantitative efficiency curves. The appendix supplies reproducibility details, targeted ablations, ScanNetV2 detection evidence, and explicit segmentation limitations while preserving the original results. These gains materially strengthen assessability and empirical support; minor appendix cross-reference errors do not outweigh them.
